summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted with severe constipation and abdominal distention after two weeks without a bowel movement. Imaging revealed significant colonic dilation consistent with Ogilvie’s syndrome, prompting placement of an NG tube and rectal tube for decompression. She developed leukocytosis, raising concern for microperforation, and was treated with Unasyn until blood cultures (positive for VRE from a femoral line) were deemed contaminants and antibiotics were discontinued. Her abdominal symptoms gradually improved, with radiographic evidence of decreasing colonic diameter. Chest pain was evaluated and ruled out as ischemic. Hypokalemia was corrected, and her ITP and heart conditions were monitored without acute intervention. She passed stool with enemas, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with home health services, continuing bowel regimen and orthopedic precautions for her right knee.
